title: Kth Smallest Element In a Bst
statement: You get the root of a binary search tree and a number k. Return the k-th smallest value in the tree, counting from 1. Assume k is between 1 and the number of nodes.

example.caption: Sorted order is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. With k = 3 the answer is 3.

idea.sentence: Visiting a search tree in order (left, node, right) gives the values sorted, so stop at the k-th visit.

jargon.plain: Visit the whole left subtree, then the node itself, then the whole right subtree. In a search tree that lists values from smallest to largest.
A list you manage yourself to remember the nodes you must come back to, instead of letting recursion remember them.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the tree as a level-order list (null for a missing child), then k. e.g. [5,3,6,2,4,null,null,1] and 3

compare.bruteLabel: Collect all values, sort, pick the k-th
compare.optimalLabel: Walk in order and stop at k

rows.name: Collect and sort
rows.note: Ignores that the tree is already ordered.

rows.name: Iterative in-order
rows.note: Dive to the leftmost node (h steps), then visit k nodes. The stack holds one path.

fast.takeaway: The tree is already sorted if you read it in order. Stop at the k-th node instead of reading everything.

stages.title: Start at the root
stages.note: cur is the node we are exploring. The stack is empty and the count is 0.

stages.title: Dive left
stages.note: Push each node and move to its left child until there is none. The top of the stack is the smallest unvisited value.

stages.title: Pop and count
stages.note: Pop the top node. It is the next value in sorted order, so add 1 to the count.

stages.title: Reached k
stages.note: If the count equals k, this node's value is the answer. Return it.

stages.title: Go right
stages.note: After a node, everything in its right subtree comes next. Move cur to the right child and dive left again.

edges.title: Single node
edges.why: Dive pushes the node, the pop makes the count 1, and 1 equals k.

edges.title: k is the largest
edges.why: You visit every node. The loop ends only at the last one, so it never stops early.

edges.title: Left chain
edges.why: The first dive pushes all four nodes. The first pop is the deepest one, which is the smallest.

edges.title: Negative values
edges.why: Sorted order is -5, -3, -1, 0, 3. Negative values are ordered like any other.

gotchas.text: Pop first, then check the count, then go right. If you move to the right child before counting, you skip the node itself.
The loop must run while cur is set OR the stack is not empty. After finishing a leaf, cur is null but the stack still has work.
k counts from 1, not from 0. Check count == k after incrementing.
stack.pop() returns TreeNode | undefined. Here the stack is never empty at that point, so a non-null assertion (!) is fine.
stack[:len(stack)-1] shrinks the slice but keeps the old node reachable in the backing array. It is harmless for a short-lived stack.

recap.key: In-order on a search tree is sorted. Dive left with a stack, pop, count, go right. Stop at k.
moves: Dive: push cur, move to cur.left
Pop a node and add 1 to count
If count == k return its value
